requirement:
During coverage-data preparation, on a terminal enabled under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.processes.progress.terminal`, Habeas MUST
display updating activity and identify the current preparation stage.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.test-coverage.processes.progress.preparation` has one clause: "During coverage-data preparation, on a terminal enabled under `requirements.test-coverage.processes.progress.terminal`, Habeas MUST display updating activity and identify the current preparation stage." It specifies only what the user sees, so it creates no structural obligation.

- **No named library, algorithm, signature, type, field or interface.** The clause doesn't name a progress library, a progress-reporter trait, a function signature or a data type.
- **Alternatives that still satisfy the text.** Take an implementation with a different progress crate, a hand-written spinner, a different delegation structure or different stage-reporting types. Any of them would still "display updating activity and identify the current preparation stage" when the terminal is enabled. So the choice of mechanism is discretionary.
- **The cited `requirements.test-coverage.processes.progress.terminal` is context only.** It defines when the terminal is enabled: stderr is interactive and `TERM` is not `dumb`. It also defines the clearing and exit-status rules. Those are also observable behavior. This review doesn't judge them, because they belong to that requirement.

No implementation roots were supplied, and none are needed. Whether the display appears and names the stage is behavioral, so test adequacy covers it.

behavioral: The subject has two obligations. During coverage-data preparation on a terminal enabled under `requirements.test-coverage.processes.progress.terminal`, Habeas MUST (1) display updating activity and (2) identify the current preparation stage. The tests cover both.

**Stage identification**
- `src/execution_coverage/progress.rs#mod[tests]/fn[stage_and_conversion_counts_are_visible_then_cleared]` uses a recording terminal. It asserts that the initial stage label "Recording inputs" is drawn. It then calls `stage("Capturing coverage maps")` and asserts the new label is drawn.
- `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[coverage_progress_on_a_pty_preserves_reports_and_plain_output_policy]` runs the real binary on a PTY with `TERM=xterm` and `NO_COLOR=1`. It asserts that stderr contains "Preparing coverage: recording inputs" and "Preparing coverage: capturing maps". The same test checks that the recording-inputs stage appears on the preparation-failure path.

**Updating activity**
- `src/execution_coverage/progress.rs#mod[tests]/fn[preparation_activity_keeps_updating_without_a_stage_change]` creates a preparation display with no stage change. It polls until at least two distinct frames containing "Recording inputs" have been recorded, with a 2-second deadline. It also asserts that every frame carries the elapsed-time marker `[00:00:`. A static, non-updating display would fail this test.
- The PTY test also asserts that escape sequences are present ("PTY progress should update in place") and that `[00:` appears in the output.

**Terminal-enabled condition**
- The PTY test runs under both `xterm` and `dumb`. Progress appears only for `xterm`, so the enabling condition is exercised. Suppression under `dumb` and with redirected stderr belongs to the cited terminal requirement, so I did not reassess it here.

All three tests carry `{test}` references to the subject, so there is no marking gap. I found no uncovered obligation.

text: During coverage-data preparation, on a terminal enabled under
display updating activity and identify the current preparation stage.
Habeas coverage progress MUST be displayed when stderr is an interactive
terminal and `TERM` is not `dumb`. `NO_COLOR` MUST disable color without
disabling progress. When stderr is redirected or `TERM=dumb`, Habeas coverage
progress MUST NOT emit animation or terminal control sequences.
Temporary progress displays MUST be cleared when their stage ends, including
empty work and early collection failures. Final diagnostics and the coverage
artifact location MUST remain readable. Progress reporting MUST NOT change
coverage results, retained profiles, or command exit status.
